simple.meaning: דַּוָּג (davvâg) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a fisherman.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Jeremiah 16:16. The surrounding context includes mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דַּוָּג (H1728) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: דַּוָּג (davvâg) / H1728 is traced through Jeremiah 16:16, Ezekiel 47:10 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H1728. davvag [ דַּיָּג ] noun masculine Ezek 47:10 fisher, fisherman , only plural דַּיָּגִים Isa 19:8 , דַּיָּגִים Qr Jer 16:16 (Kt דוגים ), דַּוָּגִים Ezek 47:10 & Kt Jer 16:16 .
definitions.rootNote: an orthographical variation of 1709 as a denominative ( 1771 );

occurrences.englishText: “Behold, I will send for many fishermen,” says Yahweh, “and they will fish them up. Afterward I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from every mountain, from every hill, and out of the clefts of the rocks.

It will happen, that fishermen will stand by it. From En Gedi even to En Eglaim will be a place for the spreading of nets. Their fish will be after their kinds, as the fish of the great sea, exceedingly many.
